anatomy.flutter: Badge(label, variant, spec?, paddingX?, minWidth?, glyph?) is a single flat-fill chip: DecoratedBox(color: _fill(theme), border, borderRadius) with no gradient layer and no shadow at all -- the doc comment states this outright: 'This port shipped that once; the project owner asked for it gone... Shadows/Surface no longer factor into this file at all.'
anatomy.web: badge.tsx: every filled variant is a flat `bg-*` fill — `ramp-chip`, `shadow-chip` and `shadow-btn-value` removed from all eight — matching badge.dart's "no need for the gradient and shadow for the badges, make them simple".
anatomy.note: CLOSED on review: the gradient and shadow were stripped from every filled variant to follow the Flutter 0.0.3 ruling, and the badge page now says so. ORIGINAL: The Flutter doc comment narrates a decision ('no need for the gradient and shadow for the badges, make them simple') that was evidently applied to the Flutter port but never landed on the web source -- components/ui/badge.tsx still ships ramp-chip and shadow-chip on every filled variant (lines 33-55), and styles/utilities.css still defines both classes as live, non-dead utilities. Whichever side is meant to be current, the two now render visibly different badges: web badges have a gradient sheen and a raised drop-shadow, Flutter badges are flat fills. File: components/ui/badge.tsx lines 28-62 vs lib/src/components/ui/badge.dart lines 1-27, 249-262.

api.flutter: BadgeVariant enum has exactly ten members in the reference's cva order: primary, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, action, premium, success, warning, info -- matching one-to-one; `paddingX`, `minWidth`, `glyph` are explicit constructor parameters (SidebarMenuBadge uses paddingX/minWidth).
api.web: Eleven variants, one-to-one with badge.dart's enum. `has-data-[icon=inline-start|inline-end]` trims padding beside a glyph the CALL SITE marks with `data-icon` — pagination.tsx and the badge page both do — so it is a working affordance, not dead code.
api.note: CLOSED on review. The finding had two halves: the variant set already matched; the "dead code" claim about the icon-inset trims was wrong — `Icon` does not write `data-icon` but callers do (grep: pagination.tsx, toast-preview.tsx, the badge page), and the selector fires for them. Verified by reading the writers, not just the one component. ORIGINAL: The variant set itself matches one-to-one (naming aside, which is a Dart-keyword rename, not a real difference). The gap is the same one recorded under anatomy: web's icon-inset padding trims (has-data-[icon=inline-*]) are dead code on the web side (Icon never writes data-icon), and the Flutter doc comment records this correctly as 'unreachable' -- but Flutter's own `glyph` parameter always applies the full px-2 padding regardless, which is consistent behaviour with what the web actually renders (not what its dead CSS rule implies), so this half is a match; recorded as api-gap only because of the ramp-chip/shadow-chip divergence carried over from the anatomy dimension, which is also an API-surface difference (the web's filled variants visually differ from what the Flutter enum's `_fill`/`_ink` maps alone can produce).

states.flutter: Badge is a StatelessWidget with no builtin hover/press state -- variant colour is the only thing that varies, and it is static per-build, not a state transition.
states.web: Badge itself declares no data-state; the only pseudo-class rules present are `[a]:hover:*`, scoped to an anchor child via `asChild`, which no corpus badge in the doc page uses.
states.note: A label chip has no state matrix of its own on either side; the `[a]:hover` rules are dead in practice per the Flutter doc comment ('the [a]:hover: rules... no badge in the corpus is a link'), consistent with the Not-ported list.

disabled.flutter: No disabled concept exists -- Badge always renders whatever variant/label it is given.
disabled.web: No disabled prop; aria-invalid: classes exist in the cva base string but are not ported (Flutter doc: 'Not ported: ... aria-invalid: -- a <span> takes none of them').
disabled.note: A badge is a passive label on both platforms; it is not a control and carries no disabled contract to compare, even though the web's unused aria-invalid: rules exist in the class string.

interaction.flutter: Not ported, by design, per the doc comment: asChild, the [a]:hover: rules, transition-all, focus-visible:, and aria-invalid: are all explicitly dropped because 'a <span> takes none of them' -- no badge in the corpus is a link.
interaction.web: badgeVariants base class carries focus-visible:border-ring, focus-visible:ring-3, aria-invalid:border-destructive, and transition-all, but Badge always renders a <span> (asChild only swaps to Slot.Root, still requiring a single interactive child to activate any of it) -- none of these classes match anything in the actual corpus, which never composes Badge as a link or form control.

semantics.flutter: Badge renders a plain StyledText inside layout widgets with no explicit Semantics wrapper -- a screen reader reads the label text as part of the surrounding content, same as an unstyled span.
semantics.web: Badge renders a plain <span data-slot="badge"> (or Slot.Root when asChild) with no implicit ARIA role beyond its text content, matching a passive inline label.
